context: Bisect which directory pair triggers it, then which module -- suspect adapters that spin up native clients at import or fixture time. Reproduce with -p no:randomly and a fixed -n value to pin the ordering, then either fix the offending import/fixture teardown or isolate that module to its own xdist group.
description: Running 'uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/utils/ tests/unit/core/runner/ tests/unit/cli/ -q' aborts a pytest-xdist worker with 'Fatal Python error: gilstate_tss_set: failed to set current tstate (TSS)'. The crash cascades into 5-7 reported FAILUREs whose membership CHANGES between identical runs -- observed sets included test_cli_test_execution + test_quiet_mode, then test_quiet_mode + test_run_driver_version_announcement, then test_platform + test_run_command_interactive_paths. Every affected file passes in isolation. Confirmed pre-existing and change-independent: reproduced on a clean tree with all working changes stashed, during PR #1304. The full fast lane (-m fast, 25775 tests) does NOT reproduce it, so CI is unaffected -- but it makes ad-hoc local subset runs untrustworthy and can send an agent chasing a phantom regression, which is exactly what it did here. Likely a native-extension/threading interaction (a C extension touching the GIL from a non-Python thread) surfaced by a particular module import order under xdist.

preserves.behavior: The fast lane keeps running under -n auto with its current worker count
